title: Repeat a slow landed CI build once and flag a persistent slowdown

intentCoverage.report:
**Caught.** The existing test detects a fault that grants the same landing's repeat allowance twice.

- **Source and revision.** `SEED-285#retry-a-slow-landed-ci-build`, its Scope and repeated-delivery/restart example, at published `c73b4d00da8228436826d95c9c0e103f9c1a086b`; canonical source `.planning/seeds/SEED-285-landed-ci-timing-history.md#retry-a-slow-landed-ci-build`, plan569. The promise is one durable allowance shared by production processes on the designated machine, without a fresh allowance after restart or duplicate delivery.
- **One fault.** In the isolated checkout's `dashboard/server/ciFollowUpAdmission.ts`, removed only `admitted.request !== undefined` from `spendRepeat`'s guard. Eligibility, authority, receipt identity, actual locked persistence, test facts and assertions stayed intact. This plausible omission forgets that an otherwise eligible landing has already spent its allowance. Exact patch and original bytes are retained under `/tmp/seed285-intent-coverage-32jb7_b4/`.
- **Fixture and maintained assertion.** `tests/support/ci-follow-up-ledger.test.mjs:47`, “two independent processes serialize spend; restart, duplicate aliases and workflow changes share one cap,” arranges existing shared MakeMe facts, enables the project and registers its receipt. Two real independent child processes call the actual allowance owner. Line55 expects their sorted answers to be `[false, true]`.
- **Reach and wrong behavior.** The faulted command reached that exact assertion and failed with actual `[true, true]`, expected `[false, true]`: both real processes were granted the same allowance. The crash-before-submission/restart case also reached line100 and failed with actual `true`, expected `false`. These are the intended cap violations, not unrelated setup errors. This check protects the allowance boundary; the earlier full-repeat journey supplies separate provider-action integration proof.

Every run used the same maintained command from the isolated checkout, with `PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH` and task-specific `OPEN_DOUGH_TEST_TIMES` / `OPEN_DOUGH_TEST_OUTCOMES` paths outside it:

`caffeinate -s -i npm test -- tests/support/ci-follow-up-ledger.test.mjs`

| Run | Maintained file outcome | Runner-reported file time | Command wall time |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Baseline | passed, exit0 | 5.2s | 5400ms |
| Fault | failed at the two cap assertions, exit1 | 4.4s | 4542ms |
| Restored | passed, exit0 | 4.9s | 5075ms |

Restoration was protected by `finally` and a termination handler. Original source bytes were restored and verified with matching SHA256 `d212ad2976b8ef36edd2d1fbc53ec834f1af2435eacc115dc3167e0757812132`. Pre/post-probe Git state matched exactly. Setup initially paused because the deliberately linked dependencies appeared as untracked `node_modules`; no test or fault had started. That owned setup link was preserved during the check and removed afterward. The clean scratch worktree was removed without force and is absent from the worktree inventory. The execution checkout was not edited by this check. All three commands reached terminal results; no check process remains.

Evidence: `/tmp/seed285-intent-coverage-32jb7_b4/result.json`, `fault.diff`, original bytes, and each run's log/times/outcomes; orchestration `/tmp/seed285-intent-coverage-probe.py`. Actual macOS pre-probe load2.13/4.78/6.07,66% free memory, AC100%; the maintained awake guard was used. No CI rerun or production repeat was requested.

- **Test runtime.** Measured: 14.5s summed maintained file durations across the three runs, rounded to tenths by the runner. Separately measured command wall total15,017ms includes the wrapper and process startup; these measures are not substituted for one another.

- **Agent effort.** Unavailable: active agent work/compute was not separately measured; the full invocation elapsed below is not substituted for it.
